sonnet.problem: The right answer is the verse's exact wording, in elevated Bible-style English. The two wrong answers are plain modern phrases, so the right one stands out.
sonnet.rule: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

sonnet.problem: Mount Perazim and the Valley of Gibeon are named with no words saying what they are. The card is only a comparison to places the baker can't place, so the moment doesn't make sense without that.
sonnet.rule: When a place, nation, false god, title or role needs explaining for the moment to make sense, he says in a few words what it is, like "Kedar, a desert tribe" or "Tammuz, a false god."
